author: Realquickpass
body: What AI says about why group debts matters:- 1. Why Fitch focuses on group gearing Fitch explicitly assesses Genting's proportionately consolidated EBITDA net leverage, not merely the standalone borrowings of Genting Bhd. It expects this ratio to remain above 4.0× for the next three years, with a possible decline below 3.5× in 2029. That is sensible for three reasons. - Economic exposure: Genting Bhd's value depends substantially on its subsidiaries, their earnings, their debt and their future investment requirements. - Cash-flow constraints: subsidiary cash must first meet operating costs, interest, debt repayments and capital expenditure before it can be distributed to the parent. - Support and contagion risk: if a subsidiary experiences financial stress, the parent may face pressure to provide support, depending on its guarantees, ownership interests and commercial incentives. Fitch's treatment is not simply adding every subsidiary's debt together and pretending Genting Bhd directly owes all of it. Its proportionate leverage methodology seeks to reflect the debt and earnings associated with the group's economic interests. 2. But group gearing is not the whole story either The strongest analysis uses both consolidated and standalone figures. Perspective What it tells us Genting Bhd standalone Whether the holding company can meet its own debt obligations Consolidated group Whether the overall operating businesses can support their debt and investment commitments Subsidiary-level analysis Where the debt sits, which assets secure it, and whether cash can move between entities For example, Genting Malaysia has its own credit rating and debt facilities. Fitch separately assessed its standalone credit profile, while also considering Genting Bhd's incentive to support it. That distinction matters because a subsidiary can have a weak credit profile without every one of its liabilities automatically becoming a direct legal liability of the parent. Conversely, a financially healthy subsidiary may not be able to distribute all its cash to the parent if it needs that money for its own debt service and expansion. 3. Does the RM1.25 billion rights issue solve the group gearing problem? Not by itself. CreditSights estimates that the rights issue would reduce Genting's pro forma net leverage by around 0.2–0.3×, to approximately 4.3×. It views the fundraising positively, but still considers the group's debt burden and capital expenditure material risks. Fitch's concern is also about the future: it forecasts average annual capex of RM9.2 billion in 2026–2028 and negative free cash flow averaging RM4 billion annually. Those projections mean that the group may continue consuming cash even after the rights issue. The critical question is whether new investments generate enough incremental EBITDA and cash flow to reverse that trend. My conclusion Yes, group gearing is generally the more realistic starting point for evaluating Genting Bhd's overall economic risk. Looking only at the parent's standalone borrowings could materially understate the risks faced by shareholders. But the best analysis does not stop at the consolidated debt figure. It reconciles the debt, cash, guarantees and cash-generating capacity of the parent and each major subsidiary. For Genting, Fitch's concern is not merely that the group has a large gross debt balance. It is that leverage may remain elevated while Singapore and New York require substantial additional investment. Until those investments produce enough cash to reduce net debt, the group's credit risk—and the possibility of a persistently depressed share valuation—remains real.

author: abc333
body: RM1.30: A Rights Issue Price or a Psychological Weapon Against Retail Investors? Genting announced an illustrative rights issue price of RM1.30. Although the final price has not yet been fixed, that number alone may be enough to anchor retail investors’ expectations. Many investors see RM1.30 and start thinking: “Why buy at RM1.42 when the price could fall further?” Fear sets in, and some may panic sell before the price even reaches RM1.30. The key point is this: the market does not need an actual RM1.30 rights issue price to trigger panic. It only needs enough investors to believe that RM1.30 is where the share price is heading. Meanwhile, LKT, through Kien Huat Realty, purchased 6 million Genting shares at RM1.494 each on October 12, representing approximately RM8.964 million. This transaction was disclosed. Now ask yourself: if retail investors panic and sell into weakness, who has the financial resources and patience to accumulate shares at lower prices? My suspicion is that LKT and his side may be willing to tolerate the downward pressure created by the rights issue — and could potentially benefit from the market panic by acquiring shares at more favourable prices. This is an inference based on the incentives and disclosed transactions, not proof of a deliberate plan. Retail investors see RM1.30 and think risk. Those with deeper pockets may see an opportunity.

author: ckwee168
body: Alenac, i believed Genting did explore selling their non core assets (i.e. Empire Resorts, Catskills and Miami Estate) but however the offer is not up to mark, and not giving the best value to shareholders .. The rising US interest rate is actually to address the overheated US market driven by AI boom and inflation (Brent above USD100/bbl), not because of an imminent recession ya .. on the contrary, if a recession is confirmed coming, the interest rate will have to come down fast to pump money into the economy .. a concern to watch here is how long the AI driven economic boom can last .. a higher interest rate environment does shorten the AI driven super cycle .. As for whether Genting can survive recession, its going to be tough and i don't have the answer .. but interest rate will also come down fast; and able to save Genting millions of dollar on restructuring of its long term financing .. US Operations are actually generating a very healthy cashflow but unfortunately runs very short to fund its aggressive CAPEX expansion .. If you have entered Genting above Rm5 previously, then it's a poor judgement ya .. but entering now ~Rm1.45 is completely a different scenario as the upside from here is huge .. market is heavily discounting Genting as they are not convinced that their aggressive CAPEX can yield the expected gains .. and if you have the same view too, then, this is not the right investment for you ..

author: MathMan
body: alenac, the value of the assets of a company is only relevant if the company is to be liquidated. The value of a going concern is the present value of all the future cash flows of that going concern. Of course, if the estimated present value of those future cash flows falls below the liquidated value of the company, consideration should be given to liquidating it -- before someone else takes over the company and does it for you.

author: MathMan
body: alenac, you asked if at RM1.45, the market is excessively discounting Genting's assets, or whether the discount reflects a genuine shortage of cash available to shareholders. An objective answer to that question is maybe, or maybe not. Because the group is so highly geared, the standard deviation of the forecast outcomes utterly overwhelms any estimate of the underlying value of the share. The distribution is wide and the mean is within a ringgit or two of zero. The key is growth. If the operational managers can squeeze some growth out of the subsidiaries, the share price contractions of the past decade might be reversed. If not, it's on a one-way trip to worthlessness. genting2030, do you disagree?

body: 他是典型的家族控制型大股东，不是职业经理人，也不是以“全体股东价值最大化”为第一优先的人。 他的核心逻辑很清楚： 公司是他的，小股东是乘客。 他可以开着这辆车去任何他想去的地方，乘客的舒适度不是优先考虑。股价三十年低位、小股东被摊薄、关联交易把家族亏本生意塞进上市公司——这些对他来说不是“问题”，而是运营家族帝国的正常成本。 他是什么样的人 1. 极度看重控制权，而不是市值。 股价跌到接近历史低位，他照样拿着集团内最高的一档薪酬（Genting Singapore 一年就有 S$750 万级别）。对他来说，薪酬是“家族应得的”，不是和股价挂钩的绩效。小股东亏钱、他照拿高薪，这个矛盾在他心里不存在。 2. 关联交易的模式已经很清晰。 Empire Resorts 就是最典型的例子：家族持有的长期亏损资产，先卖一部分给上市公司，再把剩下的也塞进去，上市公司继续输血。分析师骂、Bursa 问、股价跌，他照做。这不是偶尔一次，而是一贯做法——家族私人利益优先于上市公司少数股东利益。 3. 对小股东的态度是“礼貌但冷漠”。 股东大会上会回答 MSWG 的问题，会说“我们保护所有股东利益”，但实际决策里，小股东的声音几乎没有实质影响力。他知道自己握有足够投票权，也知道大多数小股东没有组织、没有耐心、最终会选择离开或认命。所以他不需要真正在乎他们。 4. 时机选择上的精明。 你之前提的供股时间点，和他一贯的行为是一致的。他不是冲动的人，也不是不懂市场的人。他很清楚什么时候宣布会对自己最有利——可以压低认购成本、可以在恐慌中多买一点、可以让小股东先承担下跌。这不是“巧合”，是控制权思维下的自然结果。 人性判断 LKT 不是坏人，也不是傻瓜。他是一个极度自利、极度务实、极度家族优先的控制人。 他不会为了小股东的情绪而牺牲家族利益。反过来，当家族利益和上市公司利益冲突时，他几乎总是选择前者。 对小股东来说，和他一起坐这辆车，本质上是在赌两件事： * 他最终能把生意做大，大家一起分到残羹； * 或者他某天需要市值（例如要再融资、要私有化、要退出），才会暂时对小股东好一点。 除此之外，指望他“良心发现”去优先照顾小股东，是不现实的。 你现在看到的供股时机、大跌后增持、高薪与低股价并存、关联交易反复出现——这些不是孤立事件，而是同一种人在不同场景下的同一套逻辑。 他不是来服务你的。他是来经营他自己的帝国的。小股东只是这个帝国里可以随时被稀释的部分。

author: Realquickpass
body: What AI says on Mathman statement:- Genting New York: Will table games increase profits, or simply replace slot-machine revenue? My assessment: MathMan raises a legitimate operating-risk question, but his statement is too categorical. There is no automatic profit advantage in replacing a low-cost slot-machine customer with a table-game customer. However, adding table games can expand the casino's total addressable market, increase customer spending and encourage longer visits. The crucial question for Genting New York is not whether table games are more labour-intensive. They are. It is whether the additional gaming revenue and customer spending will exceed the extra labour, operating, regulatory and financing costs. We should also distinguish replacing existing slot-machine capacity from adding a new product that attracts customers who would otherwise not visit the casino. Those are two very different economic outcomes. 1. What the actual New York operating evidence tells us The early evidence is more nuanced than MathMan's claim. Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) launched live table games on 28 April 2026, while retaining and subsequently expanding its slot-machine offering. Slot machines: still a major revenue engine During the week ending 3 May, Maybank estimated slot gross gaming revenue (GGR) at US$23.5 million, above its estimate of approximately US$19.5 million for the comparable prior-year week. This suggests the table-game launch did not immediately displace slot revenue at the property. Table games: early revenue was below expectations The 242 new tables generated about US$4.9 million in GGR over their first six days, or roughly US$3,400 per table per day. Maybank's estimate was US$7,500 per table per day. Even normalising for a lower-than-expected win rate, estimated revenue remained below that target. Later data showed the weekly table-game drop—money exchanged for chips—rose from US$34.55 million for the week ended 3 May to US$51.39 million for the week ended 9 August. Drop is not the same as GGR or profit, but it indicates growing customer activity. This is important: the initial table-game results were disappointing against expectations, but the subsequent activity trend suggests that the business was still ramping up. 2. Why table games can still be economically attractive MathMan's argument is correct only if table games mainly replace existing slot-machine play rather than generate incremental business. Consider the economics: | Factor | Slot machines | Table games | | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | | Labour | Relatively low per gaming position | Dealers, supervisors and floor staff required | | Capacity | Many machines can operate with limited staffing | Each table needs staff and sufficient player demand | | Revenue variability | Depends on play volume and hold | Depends on player turnover, stakes and hold | | Customer appeal | Convenient, fast and automated | Social experience, strategy and higher-stakes play | | Potential benefit | Efficient revenue generation | New customers, longer visits and broader market appeal | A slot machine may be more profitable per dollar of operating cost. But a table can also attract customers who prefer blackjack, baccarat, roulette or craps and would otherwise gamble at a competing casino in New Jersey, Connecticut or elsewhere. That is the strategic rationale for the expansion. RWNYC aims to retain customers who currently travel to neighbouring states for live table games, while attracting additional local and international visitors. The relevant measure is not revenue per table versus revenue per slot alone. It is incremental contribution after all additional costs, including gaming taxes, labour, marketing, utilities and other operating expenses.

author: Realquickpass
body: 3. Is cannibalisation actually happening? There are three possible outcomes. Best case New customers and incremental spending Table games attract people who previously gambled elsewhere. Slots remain busy, and total property revenue grows faster than operating costs. Mixed case Some cannibalisation, but net growth Existing slot customers shift some spending to tables, but the new product attracts enough additional customers to increase overall casino revenue and profit. Worst case Substitution without adequate growth Existing customers move from slots to tables, slot revenue falls, and the extra dealer and operating costs reduce total profitability. The first-week evidence does not establish the worst case. Maybank reported that slot revenue surged rather than collapsed, and its initial assessment suggested the publicity surrounding the new tables may have directed more gamblers to the existing machines. That said, one week is far too short to prove that cannibalisation will never occur. We need several quarters of data to distinguish launch publicity from sustainable customer growth. 4. The bigger issue for Genting shareholders: can table games generate enough EBITDA? Fitch projected that RWNYC could generate approximately US$208 million of EBITDA in 2026 and US$450 million in 2028. At the same time, it highlighted the remaining expansion spending and its pressure on the group's credit profile. These forecasts are projections, not achieved results. And EBITDA is not the same as free cash flow. For Genting, I would monitor four indicators in upcoming quarterly reports: 1. Total GGR growth: Are slots and tables together generating materially more revenue? 2. Table-game productivity: Is revenue per table approaching the operator's or analysts' assumptions? 3. Incremental EBITDA margin: How much additional operating profit remains after dealers, marketing and other expenses? 4. Cash return on capex: Can the new facilities generate sufficient cash after taxes, interest and further construction spending? The last point is especially important given Genting's leverage. A casino can report rising revenue and EBITDA while still consuming substantial cash because it is building hotels, entertainment facilities and additional gaming space. My verdict on MathMan's statement I would rate it as a valid warning about operating economics, but not a confirmed description of RWNYC's actual performance. MathMan is right that replacing profitable slot-machine activity with more labour-intensive table games can destroy value if the new tables do not bring incremental customers or spending. But RWNYC is not simply replacing its slot machines with tables. It has retained and expanded its slot capacity while adding live games, targeting customers who previously travelled to other states. The early results show table-game revenue below expectations, alongside strong slot revenue and rising table-game activity later in the summer. That supports neither unqualified optimism nor the claim that the expansion is inherently unprofitable. My investment conclusion: the NYC expansion has credible revenue-growth potential, but its ability to improve Genting's financial position remains unproven. For a highly leveraged group, the decisive test is whether incremental EBITDA turns into free cash flow quickly enough to justify the remaining capex and financing costs. Until that becomes visible in reported results, I would treat the projected earnings uplift as an opportunity with substantial execution risk—not a guaranteed solution to Genting's debt problem. MathMan The big concern with New York is the extent to which the new table games will draw patronage away from the long-standing machine-based enterprise. There's no profit in replacing a low cost automated service with a higher cost manual service.

author: MathMan
body: I would like to thank Realquickpass for the earlier posting with which I generally agree. I did not intend my posting to be interpreted as meaning that the new table games were actually drawing patronage away from the earlier slot machines. Only that if this happened, the new facilities might not turn out to be as profitable as might be needed to justify the capital expenditure. I was only trying to highlight that it was not a sure thing.

author: magnamous
body: Stop fighting for 1 minute. Important information. A generation of investors grew up believing that the company was a cash-generating machine where nothing can go wrong even during the worst of times. It survived economic turmoil and the pandemic. A stock favoured by 'mom and pops' for its regular dividends, the cash from the company's only casino in Malaysia was enough to fund its expansion overseas and keep shareholders happy. From a single casino in the Highlands, Pahang, the group, headed by its executive chairman expanded to Singapore, the UK, the US and Bahamas. The relentless expansion comes with a price. The company FELL to the lowest point in its history last week when it called for a rights issue to raise RM1.25 billion. With a cash hoard of more than RM17.6 billion and a business that draws thousands of tourists and high rollers, the company's cash call is UNFATHOMABLE. Shareholders did not take it lightly, with research analysts calling for a SELL on concerns of MORE cash calls in the FUTURE to pay off debts. Consequently, the company’s share price FELL to a 52-week low of RM1.38 last Wednesday before recovering some lost ground. The company says that there are no further cash calls being planned currently. But investors and analysts have turned NEGATIVE on the company. However, there is also a view that the rights issue is a welcome shift away from the company's traditional heavy reliance on debt funding to reduce and refinance its borrowings. It effectively indicates that shareholders are prepared to fork out money to share the deleveraging burden. However, rating agencies say that the company needs to do more than a rights issue. A sale of non-core assets is CRUCIAL to deleverage burden.

author: Daim88
body: If a substantial shareholder (like LKT) uses a rights issue to increase their shareholding from a position between 33% and 50% to over 51%, it breaches the 2% creeping threshold within a six-month period. Under the Malaysian Code on Take-Overs and Mergers and the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 (CMSA), this action triggers an immediate Mandatory General Offer (MGO) obligation Simply stating they are "exempted" in the application to Bursa Malaysia will not help them dodge the Mandatory General Offer (MGO). In Malaysia’s capital markets, Bursa Malaysia is the stock exchange that handles the listing of shares, but the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) is the supreme statutory body that regulates takeovers, mergers, and the Rules on Take-Overs. A shareholder cannot legally self-declare an exemption to bypass the law. If a shareholder attempts to circumvent the rule by merely writing a statement in the submission, the following structural checks prevent it: 1. Bursa Malaysia Will Reject the Application Bursa Malaysia closely reviews all corporate actions and additional listing applications. Under the Bursa Malaysia Listing Requirements, the company's Principal Adviser must officially verify that major shareholders have carefully considered the consequences of the rights issue regarding the Take-Overs and Mergers Code. If the numbers show the shareholder will breach the anti-creeping threshold (crossing 50% or moving by >2% in 6 months), Bursa Malaysia will halt the application until an official exemption letter from the SC is produced. 2. The SC is the Only Authority That Grants Exemptions The "Whitewash Exemption" is a strict legal process, not a checkbox. The SC must formally review and comment on the circulars, and it will only grant the exemption after the company proves it has met all statutory criteria (e.g., getting approval from non-interested minority shareholders at an EGM). 3. Deliberate Deception is a Crime If the shareholder or the company's directors falsely claim they have an exemption when they do not, it triggers Section 369 of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 (CMSA) for submitting false or misleading statements to the SC or the Exchange. This is a severe criminal offense carrying massive multi-million Ringgit fines and prison sentences.

author: Realquickpass
body: What does AI says about Genting free cashflow & ongoing capex:- Genting Bhd: Is free cash flow improving as New York table games ramp up? The key distinction is between improving casino operating performance and improving free cash flow for Genting's shareholders. Even if Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) attracts more customers and generates higher gaming revenue, Genting may still have negative free cash flow while construction spending, interest costs and other capital commitments remain high. To establish whether free cash flow is actually improving, we need to examine three layers of evidence: 1. New York casino revenue and table-game productivity. 2. RWNYC's operating earnings relative to its expansion expenditure. 3. Genting's consolidated cash flow after capital expenditure, interest and other financing requirements. The first two can indicate future improvement, but the third is what ultimately confirms it. 1. What the latest New York gaming data shows The latest detailed public gaming data I could verify, reported in October, shows a positive but mixed trend. There are three takeaways. - Table-game activity is growing. Average weekly drop increased from US$41.6 million in May to US$50.1 million in August, a rise of approximately 20.4%. - Total casino revenue is improving modestly. Weekly GGR exceeded US$30 million more consistently in July and August than in May and June. - Slot performance is less impressive. After the additional 1,400 machines opened in late July, average weekly slot GGR increased only from US$20.3 million to US$20.6 million. That is a small gain despite a substantial increase in machine capacity. The last point matters. It supports the possibility that table games are drawing some spending away from slots, or that the additional machines have not yet generated their full potential. We cannot conclude which explanation dominates without more detailed customer and profitability data. 2. Are these improvements translating into free cash flow? This is where the evidence becomes less encouraging. Genting Malaysia's second-quarter results showed that its US and Bahamas segment revenue more than doubled year-on-year to RM1.53 billion, while adjusted EBITDA rose 83% to RM216.6 million. The company attributed the improvement to the launch of full commercial casino operations at RWNYC. However, Genting Malaysia's group net profit for the first half of 2026 fell to RM43.6 million from RM489.3 million a year earlier. The company cited ramp-up costs, higher depreciation and higher financing costs associated with the development of RWNYC. 3. What Fitch says about the free-cash-flow outlook Fitch's October assessment remains cautious. It expects Genting Bhd's free cash flow to remain negative during 2026–2028, principally because of the expansion at Resorts World Sentosa, refurbishment and asset-enhancement projects, and the expansion of casino facilities in New York. It also expects Genting's proportionately consolidated EBITDA net leverage to remain elevated. This is an important distinction: - Rising GGR is encouraging. - Rising EBITDA is encouraging. - But free cash flow only improves sustainably if those gains exceed additional operating expenses, taxes, interest and capital expenditure. The US$5.5 billion RWNYC development is a multi-year project, with substantial expenditure still to come. Genting has said the financing for the required capex is in place, but that does not mean the project is already generating sufficient cash to fund all of its remaining investment.

body: Sometimes the simple answer is the best one. Perhaps the "Undertaking Shareholders" seek to avoid being obligated to make a mandatory takeover offer because they simply can't afford it or because such a large stake in a single corporation does not fit well in their portfolio or because there is a government preference that the casino license be held by a listed company. author: Realquickpass
body: I ask AI about the blame game and the answer is obvious. Those who chase or average GB shares are angry and can lead to several reactions: - Blame: investors look for management decisions, controlling shareholders or advisers to hold responsible. - Suspicion: a deeply discounted rights issue announced after a sharp share-price decline can raise questions about who benefits. - Defensiveness: some investors may strongly promote the US listing or TauRx as a way to justify holding the shares. - Anger over dilution: shareholders who lack the cash to subscribe may feel that they are being penalised for circumstances beyond their control. These reactions are understandable. But neither the losses nor the anger proves that the rights issue is improper. A. The question I would ask: is this a rescue financing or a sensible restructuring? The evidence supports a mixed answer. The case for a necessary financing exercise Genting has disclosed that RM800 million will repay borrowings falling due within 12 months, RM280 million of the working-capital allocation will cover interest and other financing costs, and the remaining funds will support general working capital and issue expenses. It expects the debt repayment to save approximately RM41.3 million in annual interest. Those are identifiable commercial purposes. They are not, by themselves, evidence of a conspiracy. The case for shareholder concern The fundraising is relatively small against group borrowings of RM45.25 billion. CIMB's illustrative analysis suggests that the new shares could materially dilute EPS, while the improvement in gearing would remain modest. So minority investors are entitled to ask whether the issue will be enough, whether further fundraising may follow and whether management can deliver adequate returns on its major capital investments. Both positions can be true: Genting may genuinely need the money, and the financing may still be unattractive for existing shareholders. B. My verdict on your interpretation I agree that some of the criticism may be driven by investors' losses and the search for someone to blame. The most useful test is to separate three things: 1. Facts: the rights issue, its disclosed uses, the controlling shareholders' undertakings and the actual share-price decline. 2. Reasonable concerns: dilution, limited interest savings, future financing requirements and the returns on capex. 3. Speculation: deliberate price suppression, an attempt to disenfranchise minorities, or a hidden strategy to transfer value to selected buyers. The first two deserve serious analysis. The third requires evidence. I would focus less on who is winning the argument online and more on whether the company can stabilise its cash flow, reduce leverage and earn adequate returns on its investments. My bottom line: There is no evidence that the controlling shareholders are conspiring against minorities. It is that Genting has a genuine financing need, and investors are questioning whether the proposed solution adequately protects their long-term interests.

author: neohts
body: TauRx helps Strictly star bust myths around online drug trend The methylene blue episode of Clickbait Clinic With Stacey Dooley will air on Monday, October 19 at 8.30pm on BBC One and can be viewed on BBC Leading Scottish life sciences firm TauRx Therapeutics Management Ltd. is to feature alongside acclaimed documentary maker and former Strictly Come Dancing winner Stacey Dooley to examine one of the latest viral wellness trends in Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley. Professor Claude Wischik, TauRx Co-Founder and Chairman, and Medical Director Dr Sonya Miller travelled to Cambridge to film scenes for Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley, which sets to air on BBC One on Monday, as well as being available now on iPlayer. Along with respected doctors and health content creators Dr Alex George and Dr Nighat Arif, Stacey examines several viral wellness trends taking over social media feeds. One of those is methylene blue, an old synthetic dye with legitimate medical uses which some people claim, when self-administered, improves cognition, prevents ageing or treats neurological disease. auRx’s potential oral treatment for Alzheimer’s disease, which is currently undergoing review by the UK’s Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), is related to methylene blue. Strictly 2018 winner Stacey gauged the expert opinions of Prof Wischik and Dr Miller on its suitability. Prof Wischik, who first discovered the Alzheimer tangle was made up of tau proteins clumped together while a PhD student at Cambridge in 1988, said: “Documentaries like Clickbait Clinic are more important than ever, particularly when it comes to health. With so much misinformation out there, we should all be programmed to maintain a healthy level of scepticism. “Only after spending many years studying the effect of methylene blue, as well as undertaking rigorous lab tests and clinical trials under strict safety protocols, have we been able to see the impact it has on the brain. “Through such work, we have established that while it plays a part in cognitive function temporarily, the effect in Alzheimer’s only happens with the new form of the drug. “The drug we have submitted to the MHRA has undergone stringent tests, and we believe the evidence available reinforces our belief it has the potential to offer an accessible oral treatment option which could be delivered safely and with minimal patient/physician burden.” As well as interviewing Prof Wischik and Dr Miller, Stacey also visits a patient who was first diagnosed with Alzheimer’s in 2013. Dr Miller added: “The documentary is extremely important in dispelling potentially dangerous online health myths. What people must realise is that you have medicines to treat the disease state of an illness and make you feel better – but if you are already well, taking the same medicine won’t necessarily improve your health further. “As a physician, I would not encourage anyone to take medical health advice from social media. If people are concerned, the first port of call should always be their GP.” As well as methylene blue, the series – which has been produced by Nutopia – also examines extreme leg-lengthening surgery, NAD+ drips and the carnivore diet to testosterone and dog deworming tablets that some believe can cure cancer. Speaking when the programme was announced, Stacey said: “Social feeds are full of health and wellness tips, but it's impossible to know which ones to believe. I can't wait to find out what the experts think and to meet the people behind the biggest online health trends.” Peer-reviewed publications report that TauRx’s drug targeting the tau protein – a key hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease – halted progression of neurodegeneration, and that participants with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) who received 16 mg/day experienced statistically significant cognitive improvement over 18 months. Participants also displayed no evidence of statistically significant cognitive or functional decline over a period of two years. Trials also confirmed the drug has a benign safety profile, with headache (1.5%) and diarrhoea (1.2%) reported as the most frequent adverse effects at the 16 mg/day dose. A decision on the company’s MHRA application is expected in the coming months.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 这篇文章为 TauRx 提供了正面的媒体曝光，也重申公司对其药物研究成果的信心；但它本质上仍是一篇带有公司宣传性质的新闻，而不是新的临床试验结果或正式审批公告。对于 TauRx 的投资价值，现阶段应把注意力放在完整临床证据、MHRA 最终决定，以及药物获批后的商业化能力，而不是单纯依赖媒体报道。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: This article provides positive media exposure for TauRx and reinforces the company’s confidence in its drug research. However, it is essentially a company-promotional news article, rather than a report of new clinical trial results or an official regulatory approval announcement. From an investment perspective, the focus should remain on the full clinical evidence, the MHRA’s final decision, and TauRx’s ability to commercialise the drug if approved, rather than relying solely on media coverage.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: A Question for ATK Clown: Why Keep Promoting the US IPO Story? You reportedly hold only 5,000 shares, yet you keep promoting LKT's US IPO story as though it is almost a certainty. Why? What is the basis for your confidence that LKT will file for a US IPO in June 2027? Where is the official announcement, the confirmed timetable, or the evidence to support your prediction? RWNYC is still under construction. The projected peak EBITA has not yet been fully demonstrated, and filing for an IPO does not guarantee that the listing will succeed. Look at Olam Group and ThaiBev. Both have discussed IPO plans for years, yet their respective IPO stories have been repeatedly delayed. Why should investors assume RWNYC will be different? Holding 5,000 shares.... But why present speculation as if it were a confirmed plan? Are you sharing an evidence-based investment analysis, or simply selling investors another exciting story? If your prediction is correct, the facts will eventually prove it. If you are wrong, investors who believed your claims may be the ones who pay the price. ATK Clown, less storytelling, more evidence. Investors deserve facts, not hype.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: How many IPO stories have we heard over the years that never materialised? 1) Olam Group — ofi IPO For years, Olam has talked about listing its food ingredients business. Yet the IPO remains uncompleted. Debt reduction and asset sales may be progress, but promises of value creation are not the same as delivery. 2) ThaiBev — BeerCo IPO ThaiBev has repeatedly discussed listing its beer business, only to postpone the IPO several times. There is still no confirmed listing date. Years of promises, and investors are still waiting! So, what about the RWNYC IPO story? ATK Clown predicts that LKT will file for a US IPO in June 2027, using interim peak EBITA figures. The full resort expansion in 2029 will then provide the growth story for the IPO. But RWNYC's expansion is still underway, and future EBITA figures remain projections. Filing for an IPO does not guarantee a successful listing. Forecast EBITA is not actual earnings! ATK Clown, the IPO dream machine! RWNYC is still under construction, Yet the IPO story is already in circulation. The resort isn't even fully built, But the IPO blueprint is already filled! ATK Clown, stop selling dreams as facts! Every time you promote a story, you make it sound spectacular — turning forecasts into facts, possibilities into certainties, and leaving TauRx followers hanging on every word. ATK Clown, ATK Clown, Stop relying on stories alone! Put the facts and figures on display, Let investors judge the case their own way! ATKClown, ATKClown, Investors deserve the truth! Dreams are free, and promises are cheap, But neither guarantees the returns investors seek! We've seen this movie before: IPO promises, repeated delays, and investors left waiting. Until the filing happens and the numbers are real, it's just another story — not a result

body: At around the time when bids were being made for the Macau casinos, the dynamic in the casino industry changed from balanced investment to borrowing at ZIRP rates and capitalising for all its worth. The companies that won licenses did so by offering to invest truly stratospheric amounts of borrowed money. But ZIRP is now RIP and the grim reaper is seeking his revenge. Interest rates are increasing and refinancing all that borrowed money is no longer possible at the originally budgeted interest rates. It seems likely that there will be casualties. Whether Genting Berhad can, metaphorically speaking, do a double back-flip with an inverted pirouette remains to be seen.

author: Realquickpass
body: Yes Mathman, 2022 Macau experience capital allocation and debt-cycle risk even at ZIRP rates and succeeding refinancing. The Macau experience illustrates how licence competition can encourage very large investment promises. Genting's current situation illustrates a related problem: several major expansion programmes can overlap, creating a period in which cash expenditure rises well before the expected earnings arrive. For GB shareholders, the critical issue is no longer simply whether Resorts World New York or Resorts World Sentosa will succeed commercially. It is whether the group can finance the journey to those future earnings without repeatedly increasing debt or diluting shareholders. Given the projected RM4 billion annual negative FCF and the proposed RM1.25 billion rights issue, I would treat further financing needs as a material risk in any assessment of GB's share price. The next decisive evidence will be whether actual operating cash flow improves fast enough to bring leverage down before 2029.

author: Daim88
body: To annul or terminate a proposed rights issue during an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM), minority shareholders must successfully defeat the relevant resolutions by voting AGAINST them. When a company proposes a corporate action like a rights issue, it requires shareholder approval through voting resolutions. If minority shareholders vote "AGAINST" or "NO", and the resolution fails to reach the required voting threshold, the rights issue cannot proceed and is effectively terminated. Voting Strategy for Minority Shareholders Based on the resolutions you provided, here is how minority shareholders typically coordinate to block a rights issue and protect their interests: • Resolution 1 (Proposed Rights Issue): Vote AGAINST/NO. This directly denies the company the authority to issue new shares. • Resolution 2 (Whitewash Waiver for Mandatory General Offer): Vote AGAINST/NO. A whitewash waiver allows a major shareholder (like the controlling family or executive group) to increase their stake past a certain threshold without triggering a Mandatory General Offer (MGO) to buy out all other shareholders. • Inherent Voting Restrictions: Under most capital market regulatory frameworks (such as the Securities Commission or Stock Exchange listing rules), interested parties—such as "LKT", the controlling family, and conflicted executives—are considered interested directors/major shareholders and are strictly interested parties barred from voting on the Whitewash Waiver resolution. This gives independent minority shareholders maximum leverage. • Other Resolutions: Voting AGAINST/NO on all subsequent or related resolutions ensures there are no alternative pathways or amendments approved that could bypass the main rejected resolutions. Key Protections: Demanding a Poll Vote To ensure the voting process is completely fair and to prevent any manipulation or "cheating," shareholders have the legal right to monitor the vote count closely: 1. Demand a Poll Vote: Ensure the chairman conducts the voting via a poll vote rather than a show of hands. A poll vote calculates results based on the exact number of shares held, ensuring every share's weight is accurately reflected. 2. Scrutineers: EGMs typically employ independent scrutineers to oversee, count, and validate the proxy forms and physical/digital votes. Shareholders have the right to ask who the independent scrutineers are during the Q&A session. 3. Protest and Reporting: If there are discrepancies or suspicious voting activities, shareholders can formally lodge a complaint during the meeting to be recorded in the minutes, or subsequently report the matter to the national securities regulator or company registrar.

author: Johnchew123
body: Affin Hwang Investment Bank analyst Andrew Lim downgraded Genting and Genting Malaysia to “Sell” from “Hold”, cutting their target prices to RM1.10 from RM2.30 and RM1.00 from RM1.80, respectively. These imply approximately 25.2% and 21.3% downside, respectively. He believes Genting’s proposed RM1.25 billion rights issue offers limited debt relief, as the RM800 million earmarked for repayment represents less than 2% of its RM45.3 billion group borrowings. Substantial ongoing investment commitments also raise concerns over medium-term funding visibility. Looking ahead, Andrew remains cautious on Genting Malaysia’s New York investment commitments, citing Fitch’s estimate of approximately US$3.7 billion in remaining investment over five years. Although full-scale casino operations offer longer-term growth potential, heavy upfront spending, higher operating costs and a potentially slower earnings ramp-up could delay meaningful free cash flow. Andrew also highlighted recent credit-rating downgrades as evidence of reduced financial flexibility amid elevated leverage, substantial capital commitments and a slower-than-expected earnings recovery. Fitch lowered Genting Malaysia’s issuer rating to BBB− from BBB in September 2026, leaving it at the lowest investment-grade level. Domestic recovery also remains subdued, with Resorts World Genting’s hilltop visitation falling 3% year-on-year in 1H26. He left underlying earnings forecasts unchanged, but adopted more conservative valuation assumptions and incorporated potential dilution from Genting’s illustrative rights issue. He also downgraded the gaming sector to “Underweight”, reflecting concerns over elevated leverage, reduced financial flexibility, heavy investment commitments and subdued near-term earnings.

body: RWNYC must pay additional $150 million annually for racing support outside its current 56% slot machine tax rate. Governor Kathy Hochul argues it must be paid separately, which would spike the effective slot tax rate to 72%. Following the launch of full commercial casino operations (including live table games) in April 2026, the ramp-up costs and heavy capital expenditure (aimed at scaling EBITDA toward $200M–$300M by FY2027) have compressed Genting Malaysia's near-term group profits. author: MathMan
body: Before assuming that all the capital investment was motivated by sound financial reasoning, consider the possibility that it was simply necessitated by the business imperative of having to keep the casino licenses, especially in Singapore and New York. I.e. that the governments of Singapore and New York simply said that if you want to keep (or get) your casino license you have to invest more. If the motivation was the former, it may well be that future returns are on the way. If it was the later, the incremental profits may not be sufficient to show an adequate return on the capital. If the net present value of the cost of the debt exceeds the net present value of the earnings of the business, the value of a share becomes negative.

author: abc333
body: The racing support issue is indeed a major hurdle for RWNYC's expansion. Anyhow, According to the New York legislation, the temporary arrangement took effect on June 5, 2026, and is valid for one year — meaning it is expected to expire around June 5, 2027, not December 2026. Unless there is a separate financing, construction or regulatory deadline, there is no confirmed basis to say Genting must resolve the issue by December to avoid expansion delays. That said, the issue remains a significant overhang. If Genting secures a favorable agreement with the state authorities before the temporary arrangement expires, it could improve the project's cash flow visibility, financing conditions and valuation. The key is to distinguish between a potential December catalyst and the actual June 2027 expiry of the temporary arrangement.

author: metaverse
body: "Life is like a box of chocolates—you never know what you’re gonna get" I joined this forum when Genting was trading at RM2.10. I came here to share a simple story, a structural downtrend seldom stops at the second floor, the price initially ejected from RM2.10 to RM2.38, everyone was happily partying in the rain with the false illusion of the Christmas drug story of TauRx, I said watch the high-volume long-tail shooting star. People laughed, as a famous stock DJ was shouting "Strong Buy", target price RM2.88 so everyone was chasing RM2.38. Today, the same stock DJ is whispering "Strong Sell", target price RM1.00. Apparently, this famous stock DJ can change his story faster than a snake sheds its skin. Fast forward the story to early September, Genting was trading around RM1.88, I shifted gear, because I saw hidden Gremlin hand quietly grabbing lot of shares and Oct might have big news. If the RI is to be fixed at RM1.30, then RM1.88 remains a possible target by Q1 2027, so it is still too early to declare RM1.88 will never arrive. Possibly MM is an engineer by training so his trading blueprint remains the same through out the time, but life never moves in a straight line and has no fixed playbook and full of surprise. 2.2 → 2.05 → 1.96 → 1.88 → 1.80 → 1.71 → 1.56
